outcomes: On a hosted run, no repository-controlled process can read a credential: not in its environment, the user's home, the workspace, or the memory of the engine and its providers
A cold install of a private CLI pin works from an empty store and leaves every locked file unchanged
nonGoals: Base-image pulls in container package jobs; they move to in-process transfers with the publication pipeline
The producers: the cloud credential-provider, its cache authenticate handler, and the hosted runner that passes --credential-fd
Denying inspection on macOS, which has no same-user /proc and restricts task_for_pid

requirements.text: --credential-fd <n> names an inherited descriptor, 3 or more, holding the run credential on one line. The engine reads and closes it before it starts a process, keeps the bearer in memory, drops the cache and cloud tokens, and on Linux turns non-dumpable. A pin relaunch passes it on a new descriptor and refuses a pin below its custody level. A user-scope provider alone serves the pinned CLI and extension downloads before the workspace provider. A bound request takes the flag as its only argument.

The engine hands the run credential to its providers over their RPC, never in their environment: a credential-provider in the initialize runCredential member, a cache provider through the authenticate operation after both sides negotiate the run-credential capability. Without a run credential both messages are byte-identical to before.

On a hosted run, putnami install runs every extension's workspace-fetch job to completion before any workspace-install: the store extensions' fetch first, then the remote cache provider's authenticate, then the path extensions' fetch. Only a store extension's workspace-fetch job run by its extension's runtime receives the read credential, on the descriptor PUTNAMI_JOB_CREDENTIAL_FD names. Every other job and hook runs with PUTNAMI_OFFLINE_DEPENDENCIES=1 and no credential, and no installer writes one into the user's home. Only the store extensions' fetch carries PUTNAMI_HOSTED_FETCH=1, and a CLI started with it refuses to run.

On a hosted run, a postinstall script and a test running as the same user search their environment, the user's home, the temporary directory, the workspace, and on Linux the /proc environ and memory of the engine and its providers and a ptrace attach. None of them finds the run credential or the read credential. The run executes only extensions installed from the artifact store, downloaded from a registry the runner chooses, never one the workspace declares by name. It also runs the workspace's own path extensions, which serve no provider and start only after the last handoff of the credential. It probes no toolchain inside the workspace.

A hosted install of a workspace that pins a private CLI different from the one that starts the run works from an empty store. The sha256 of bun.lock, .npmrc and putnami.lock.json is unchanged and git status --porcelain is empty afterwards.

Without --credential-fd the engine reads no descriptor, every job and hook environment is the same as before, putnami install runs no workspace-fetch job, and every provider message is byte-identical to before.
